decision.note: Priority is inherited from the portfolio registry and is independent of repository quality.

strengths: The project has a clear Public Reading Archive / Private Reading Lab product split and evidence-first architecture.
Exact audited HEAD passed 130 tests on Python 3.11 and Python 3.13.
The latest Pages-changing commit completed the Pages deploy successfully, including public artifact validation and inline JavaScript syntax checking.
All observed third-party GitHub Actions are pinned to immutable commit SHAs after remediation.
Ten JSON schemas and extensive regression coverage make high-level analysis contracts executable rather than documentation-only.
Publication policy, AGENTS guidance, Pages documentation, and ecosystem documentation were aligned to one canonical publication boundary.
Legacy A1 category double-counting now uses the shared union-by-bookId metric and Issue #1 was closed.

findings.title: Personal WeRead exports remain tracked in the public repository
evidence: The audited tree still tracks data/weread_notes_export.json, data/weread_notes_export.md, data/weread_readdata.json, data/weread_notebooks.json, data/weread_shelf.json, data/weread_progress.json and data/weread_bookinfo.json.

.gitignore now classifies data/weread_*.json, data/weread_*.md and data/analysis/* as local/private by default, so the current tracked state is intentionally grandfathered rather than the desired default.
Issue #2 explicitly tracks current-branch and history cleanup.
The repository owner explicitly chose on 2026-09-16 not to clean the personal data yet.
findings.recommendation: Preserve this as an accepted risk for now. Re-open cleanup before broader redistribution or when the owner authorizes current-tree removal/history rewrite; never rewrite history automatically.

findings.title: GitHub Actions used mutable major-version tags
evidence: Before remediation, both workflows referenced actions/checkout@v7 and actions/setup-python@v7; Pages also used configure-pages@v6, upload-pages-artifact@v5 and deploy-pages@v5.
All seven observed references are now pinned to full immutable commit SHAs with version comments.
Python 3.11 and 3.13 tests passed after the pinning change, and the Pages workflow successfully deployed on the Pages-changing commit.
findings.recommendation: Keep action upgrades explicit and reviewed; advance pins only after the test and Pages gates pass.

findings.title: Publication/privacy documentation had contradictory old and new rules
evidence: Older AGENTS/pages/ecosystem text described the public site as synthetic-only while the active workflow and README published a bounded real-data archive.
docs/publication-policy.md is now the canonical publication source of truth and AGENTS.md, docs/pages.md and docs/ecosystem.md were aligned to it.
findings.recommendation: Treat docs/publication-policy.md as canonical and re-audit whenever public/private switches or validators change.

findings.title: Legacy A1 analysis double-counted books present in both shelf and notes
evidence: Issue #1 documented the duplicate-counting behavior in legacy scripts/analysis.py.
scripts/analysis.py now calls metrics.category_participation(), which counts the union of unique bookId values and has regression coverage.
The post-fix exact HEAD passed 130 tests on Python 3.11 and 3.13; Issue #1 was closed as completed.
findings.recommendation: Keep legacy analysis frozen and route future deterministic metrics through scripts/metrics.py.

findings.title: main branch is not protected
evidence: GitHub branch metadata for main returned protected=false with no required status checks.
findings.recommendation: If the repository is treated as a stable public product, enable protected-main rules and require the test matrix before merge.

findings.title: Public repository has no software license
evidence: GitHub metadata reports license=null and the repository tree has no LICENSE file.
findings.recommendation: Choose a license only when the owner decides the intended reuse rights; do not infer MIT/Apache automatically.

findings.title: GitHub repository profile metadata is empty
evidence: GitHub repository metadata returns description=null, homepage=null and topics=[].
The project already has a live GitHub Pages URL and a strong README, so discoverability metadata is the missing layer rather than project positioning.
findings.recommendation: Apply a concise description, the GitHub Pages homepage, and relevant topics in repository settings.

limitations: The repo-auditor HTTP collector could not directly resolve api.github.com from the execution sandbox; the same collector evidence fields were gathered through the authenticated GitHub connector instead.
A real private-data end-to-end WeRead API run was not executed in this audit.

The exact audited HEAD did not re-run Pages because its final changes were outside the Pages path filter; the immediately preceding Pages-changing commit 2fabc220c3b5df6bf35ea3c86a8db44eceef4c77 completed the deploy successfully.
This audit is not a copyright, privacy-law, or security certification.
recheck_triggers: Any change to docs/publication-policy.md or the public/private publication switches.
Any change to scripts/validate_pages_output.py or the Pages workflow.
Owner authorization to remove tracked personal data or rewrite repository history.
Any new remote write capability to WeRead.
A license decision, first tagged release, or branch-protection change.
Material changes to the shared fact layer, schemas, or Private Reading Lab architecture.

reasons: The repository is already public, so changing visibility later would not erase prior disclosure.

The codebase and validated Public Reading Archive are suitable for a public layer, while raw personal exports are better treated as a private/local evidence layer when the owner later authorizes that separation.
No employer/client/PI ownership or patent-sensitive mechanism blocker was identified in this audit; this is not legal clearance.

evidence: README and supporting docs clearly define Public Reading Archive, Private Reading Lab, evidence semantics, and non-claims.
Exact audited HEAD passed 130 tests on Python 3.11 and 3.13; Pages deploy/validation passed on the latest Pages-changing commit.
A real private-data end-to-end API run was outside this audit.
Public/private Page boundaries are backed by validators and a canonical publication policy, but full personal WeRead exports remain tracked in the public repository as an explicitly accepted risk.
All observed GitHub Actions are pinned to immutable commit SHAs after remediation.
Optional legacy analysis dependencies remain version-unlocked and there is no general lockfile.
Core tests run on Python 3.11 and 3.13 and much of the current pipeline uses the standard library; schemas and deterministic builders are committed.
No lockfile exists and full real-data/private-lab reproduction requires user-local data/API access.
GitHub Pages build/deploy and artifact validation are automated, but main is unprotected, there is no LICENSE, and there is no formal tagged-release/changelog surface.
README, AGENTS, ecosystem, Pages, publication policy, skill landscape and skill audit provide unusually complete product and architecture guidance.
The repository has 40 test modules, 10 schemas, shared deterministic metrics and aligned documentation; the known legacy A1 bug was removed rather than merely documented.
README, Issues and SECURITY.md exist, but description/homepage/topics are empty and LICENSE/CONTRIBUTING/CHANGELOG/CITATION are absent.
